zh: 6.1　论装饰艺术
en: 6.1　On Decorative Art

zh: 由于这些关于艺术的反思主要是面向现有的艺术人类学同行圈子，我可以首先考察艺术人类学文献中的一个经典主题——即“几何”（亦即无再现性或只有少许再现成分的）装饰纹样的意义——以此开篇，或许也算是一种补偿。大多数“西方”艺术理论谈论的是再现性艺术，艺术哲学的大部分也是如此——就这两者可以区分而言。但可以公允地说，民族学博物馆收藏的艺术品大半是“装饰”艺术，哪怕这类藏品未必会陈列出来，通常施加于陶罐、席子之类的人工制品上。关注艺术的人类学家所产出的许多较有趣的研究（如 Kaeppler 1978; Hanson 1983; Price and Price 1980）都与这类艺术有关。无疑，非西方艺术研究中最庞大的资料汇编（Carpenter and Schuster 1986）主要处理的也是表面上的装饰艺术，尽管这些作者的方法以这样的观念为前提：看似装饰性的形式具有普遍的象征意义。
en: Since these reflections on art are directed in the main at the existing anthropology-of-art confraternity, I can make a start—and perhaps make amends—by considering, first of all, a classical theme in the anthropology-of-art literature, namely, the significance of ‘geometric' (i.e. non-representational, or marginally representational) decorative designs. Most ‘Western' art-theory is about representational art, and so is most of the philosophy of art, in so far as these two may be distinguished. But it is fair to say that most of the art in the collections held in ethnological museums-if not on display there-is 'decorative' art, usually applied to artefacts such as pots, mats, and so forth. Many of the more interesting studies which have been produced by anthropologists concerned with art (e.g. Kaeppler 1978; Hanson 1983; Price and Price 1980) have to do with this kind of art. Certainly the most massive compilation of data for the study of non-Western art (Carpenter and Schuster 1986) deals primarily with ostensibly decorative art, though these authors' approach is predicated on the idea that apparently decorative forms have universal symbolic meaning.

zh: 以考察装饰艺术来开始“艺术人类学”的实质性讨论还有另一个理由，那就是消除许多艺术人类学文献（包括本书）中普遍存在的一种性别偏见：它们最关注的是男性主导的艺术生产语境，如男性专属的崇拜仪式。正是在由男性组成的祭祀团体或由男性主导的崇拜活动中，艺术生产以与西方“纯艺术”最直接可比的形式出现；但这并不构成在分析上总是把这类艺术生产置于首位的理由。二十世纪（西方）抽象艺术的发展，以及“设计”同时崛起至与纯艺术声望相当甚至更高的地位，表明了一种态度的转变，这种转变也可以扩展到非西方艺术家所生产的非再现性艺术和／或“设计”。在世界范围内，许多乃至大多数装饰艺术家是女性，因为农业／自给型生计社会的劳动分工常常把纺织、制陶、编篮之类分配给女性。这并不是说没有男性装饰艺术家。然而，从装饰艺术开始的好处在于，我们仿佛置身于一块中立地带，而不像许多高地位仪式艺术那样，处于被激烈的意识形态与制度争斗所撕裂的地带。
en: There is another reason for commencing the substantive discussion of ‘the anthropology of art' with a consideration of decorative art, and that is the elimination of a form of gender bias which is prevalent in much of the anthropology-of-art literature (this work included), which pays most attention to contexts of art production dominated by men, such as gender-exclusive male cult rituals. It is in the context of male cults, or cult activities dominated by men, that art production occurs in forms which bear the most immediate comparison with Western ‘fine' art; but this is no reason for always giving this type of art production pride of place, analytically. The development of (Western) abstract art during the twentieth century, and the simultaneous rise of ‘design' to a status rivalling, or even exceeding, the prestige of fine art, indicates a change in attitude which may also be extended to the non-representational art and/or ‘design' produced by non-Western artists. Many, even most, decorative artists world-wide are women, because of the frequency with which the division of labour in agrarian/subsistence societies assigns textile production, pottery, basketry, and the like, to women. Which is not to say that there are not male decorative artists as well. The advantage of beginning with decorative art, however, is that we are, so to speak, in a neutral terrain, not one riven with violent ideological and institutional tussles, as is the case with much high-status ritual art.

zh: 6.2　附着
en: 6.2　Attachment

zh: 施加于人工制品上的装饰纹样使人附着于物，并附着于这些物所关联的社会计划。孩子往往不愿意上床睡觉，但如果床上的床单和枕套缀满了飞船、恐龙、甚至波点图案——只要足够欢快、足够吸引人——孩子就更容易被哄上床。物的装饰是一种社会技术的组成部分，我在别处称之为魅惑技术（Gell 1992b）。这种心理技术鼓励并维持社会生活所必需的动机。世界上之所以充满装饰过的物，是因为装饰往往对人工制品的心理功能至关重要，而这种心理功能与它们拥有的其他功能类型——尤其是实用功能或社会功能——不可分离。没有装饰的儿童床单在提供睡眠中的保护与舒适方面，功能会差一些，因为孩子更不愿意睡在上面。它们的社会功能也会差一些，因为舒适、受保护、安睡的婴儿是父母追求的首要目标。换言之，我们在“纯粹”装饰与功能之间所作的区分是没有根据的；装饰内在地具有功能性，否则它的存在就无法解释。
en: Decorative patterns applied to artefacts attach people to things, and to the social projects those things entail. A child may more readily be induced to go to bed---which children are often disinclined to do-if the bed in question has sheets and a pillowcase richly embellished with spaceships, dinosaurs, or even polka dots, be they sufficiently jolly and attractive. The decoration of objects is a component of a social technology, which I have elsewhere called the technology of enchantment (Gell 1992b). This psychological technology encourages and sustains the motivations necessitated by social life. The world is filled with decorated objects because decoration is often essential to the psychological functionality of artefacts, which cannot be dissociated from the other types of functionality they possess, notably their practical, or social functionality. Undecorated children's bedsheets would be less functional in conferring protection and comfort during sleep than decorated ones because children would be less inclined to sleep in them. They would be less socially functional, because comfortable, protected, sleeping infants are a prime objective pursued by parents. In other words, the distinction we make between ‘mere' decoration and function is unwarranted; decoration is intrinsically functional, or else its presence would be inexplicable.

zh: 任何大小形状合适的竹筒或容器都可以充当石灰罐，比如我在[

]中展示的亚特穆尔（新几内亚）石灰罐。但一个素面的容器恐怕不会同样有功能，因为在亚特穆尔社会生活的语境中，男人的石灰罐是其所有者人格的极其重要的索引。例如，在石灰罐中摇响石灰棒是演说表演中传达激烈情感的手段（Bateson 1973; Forge 1973）。独特的装饰以最亲密的方式把石灰罐与其所有者紧密联结起来；它与其说是一件财产，不如说是一件假体，一个经由制造和交换而非生物生长获得的身体器官。人格在人工制品和交换物品中的对象化是一个熟悉的人类学主题，无须赘述（如 Munn 1973, 1986; M. Strathern 1988）。然而，人类学尚未对由表面装饰中介的人与物之间的附着性质进行理论化，而这才是摆在我们面前的任务，而不是提供更多的民族志语境。检查这个葫芦容器，我们可以看到它装饰着美丽的纹样，由并不明显类似于现实世界对象的母题构成。葫芦的装饰是对曲线、椭圆、螺旋与圆圈的自由运用，以对称或重复的方式排列。到目前为止，我还没有谈论索引的对称、优雅等表面上的“审美”特征，人们可能以为我既然预先排除了对艺术品的“审美”进路，就根本不打算谈这些。然而这会是一个错误，因为我前面提到的“魅惑技术”进路（即艺术人类学的心理学方面）把社会效力理论与一些考量结合在一起，这些考量即便不是审美的，也无疑是认知性质的，因为认知与社会性是一体的。
en: Any bamboo tube, or container of suitable size and shape, could do duty as a lime-container, such as the ones I illustrate in

from the Iatmul (New Guinea). But a plain container would hardly be as functional, given that a man's lime-container, in the context of Iatmul social life, is a most important index of its owner's personhood. For instance, rattling the lime-stick in the lime-container is a means of communicating passionate emotion in oratorical performances (Bateson 1973; Forge 1973). The decoration, which is distinctive, binds the lime-container to its owner in a most intimate fashion; it is less a possession than a prosthesis, a bodily organ acquired via manufacture and exchange rather than by biological growth. The objectification of personhood in artefacts and exchange items is a familiar anthropological theme, on which it is unnecessary to dwell (e.g. Munn 1973, 1986; M. Strathern 1988). However, anthropology has yet to theorize the nature of the attachment between persons and things mediated by surface decoration, and that, rather than the provision of a more ethnographic context, is the task before us. Examining this gourd container, we are able to see that it is decorated with beautiful patterns, formed from motifs that do not obviously resemble real-world objects. The gourd's decoration is a free exercise in the deployment of curves, ovals, and spirals and circles, in symmetrical or repetitive arrangements. So far, I have not said anything about such ostensibly ‘aesthetic' features of the index as symmetry, elegance, etc. and it might have been assumed that I never intended to, having ruled out the ‘aesthetic' approach to the work of art in advance. This would be a mistake, however, since the ‘technology of enchantment' approach which I alluded to before (which is the psychological aspect of the anthropology of art) conjoins a theory of social efficacy with considerations which, if not aesthetic, are definitely cognitive in nature, because cognition and sociality are one.

zh: 如何把这些认知考量整合进迄今推进的理论框架——四个基本项（索引、艺术家、原型、接受者）、施动者／受动者关系等等？假定就装饰纹样而言，要么没有原型，要么原型不显著，那么“纹样”与索引就是同一个东西，这意味着整个讨论只能围绕艺术家、索引、接受者展开。对于处理复杂的认知问题、甚至可能的审美问题来说，这似乎是一套相当有限的概念。如何做到这一点呢？
en: How can such cognitive considerations be integrated into the theoretical framework advanced hitherto-the four basic terms, index, artist, prototype, recipient, agent/patient relationships, and so on? On the assumption that, where decorative patterns are concerned, there either is no prototype, or the prototype is not salient, the ‘pattern' and the index are one and the same, which would imply that the whole discussion would have to be carried out in terms of artist, index, and recipient. This seems a rather limited set of concepts for handling complicated cognitive, even possible aesthetic, problems. How may this be accomplished?

zh: 6.3　装饰纹样＝索引-A → 索引-P
en: 6.3　Decorative Pattern = Index-A → Index-P

zh: 在上文第3.10节中，我确立了这样一个观念：我们从索引中得出的能动性溯因推理，包括索引的各部分相对于索引其他部分的施动者／受动者关系。因此，在一幅抽象画中，一块颜色似乎在“推挤”另一块颜色，尽管我们无法把这些色块对应到外部世界里的任何对象。我们感知到的因果互动内在于索引本身。索引内部部分与部分之间的“因果互动”正是“装饰”艺术的基础，而装饰艺术不过是抽象艺术的另一个名称。使用“纹样”的装饰艺术利用了母题的重复与对称排列所产生的特别（视觉上）显著的部分间关系。
en: In Section 3.10 above, I established the idea that among the abductions of agency we derive from the index are agent patient relationships between parts of the index vis-à-vis other parts of the index. Thus, in an abstract picture, one patch of colour seems to be ‘pushing against' another patch of colour, even though there are no objects in the external world with which we can identify these patches of colour. The causal interaction we perceive is internal to the index itself. Part-to-part ‘causal interaction' internal to the index is the basis of ‘decorative' art, which is just another name for abstract art. Decorative art involving the use of ‘patterns' exploits the particularly (visually) salient part-to-part relationships produced by the repetition and symmetrical arrangement of motifs.

zh: 把装饰纹样施加于人工制品，会成倍增加其部分的数量及其内部关系的密度。[
]中的石灰罐若没有装饰，就会是缺乏显著部分—整体关系的简单管状形式。而实际上，可以区分出许多独立的部分，以及这些部分之间的关系。这些部分中的每一个都可以被视为整体索引之内的一个从属索引。
en: The application of a decorative pattern to an artefact multiplies the number of its parts and the density of their internal relationships. The lime-containers in

, were they lacking in decoration, would be simple tubular forms lacking in salient part-to-whole relationships. As it is, many separate parts may be distinguished, and relationships between these parts. Each of these parts may be considered a subordinate index within the index as a whole.

zh: 索引的部分正如作为整体的索引一样传达能动性。就装饰艺术而非再现艺术而言，传达重要艺术能动性的不是部分的多样性，而是部分彼此的配置。换言之，索引的各部分彼此施加因果影响，并证明作为整体的索引的能动性，因为艺术家的能动性主要正是在索引各部分的配置中显现出来的。我们确实习惯于把装饰过的表面（以及包含大量身体动作的再现性索引）说成“有生命的”。这一习语反映了这样一个事实：装饰艺术中的母题往往确实像是在跳一场迷宫般的舞蹈，我们的眼睛很容易在其中迷失。我们需要一个公式来捕捉装饰形式中内在的能动性——这些形式不只是指涉（再现）外部世界中的能动性，而是在索引自身的物理身体中生产能动性，使它无需摹仿任何生物就成为“活物”。装饰以非再现的方式使物活起来。由于这一效果是经由索引内部的部分—整体关系完成的，装饰索引可用[
]来表示，也可写成：
en: Parts of indexes convey agency just as indexes as wholes do. In the case of decorative art as opposed to representational art, it is not the diversity of the parts that communicates significant artistic agency, but their disposition with respect to one another. In other words, the parts of the index exert causal influence over one another and testify to the agency of the index as a whole, in that it is in the disposition of the parts of the index that the artist's agency is primarily made apparent. We are, indeed, accustomed to speak of decorated surfaces (as well as representational indexes with a lot of physical action in them) as ‘animated'. This idiom reflects the fact that the motifs in decorative art often do seem to be engaged in a mazy dance in which our eyes become readily lost. We need a formula which captures the inherent agency in decorative forms, forms which do not simply refer to (represent) agency in the external world, but which produce agency in the physical body of the index itself, so that it becomes a ‘living thing' without recourse to the imitation of any living thing. Decoration makes objects come alive in a non-representational way. zh: 纹样的根是母题，母题与相邻母题建立关系，这些关系使作为整体的索引活起来。然而，我们可以更精确地描述纹样中相关的部分间与部分—整体关系。纹样之所以能与所有其他索引区分开来，在于它们具有重复与对称这一显著的视觉属性。
如果以为对称与重复既然是形式的数学属性，那么就恰恰不是这些属性最容易在索引中引发内在因果性的幻觉——即便它只是幻觉——那就错了。没有什么比伊斯兰装饰工匠和书籍泥金装饰师设计的密铺图案（铺砌纹样）更有生命感了。宗教强加的禁止再现生物形体的禁令，似乎反而激发了越来越有效的、以视觉巧艺诱发摄魅的手段，让纹样不经摹仿便显得具有生命。
en: The root of a pattern is the motif, which enters into relationships with neighbouring motifs, relations which animate the index as a whole. However, we can describe the relevant part-to-part and part-to-whole relationships in patterns much more precisely. Patterns can be distinguished from all other indexes by virtue of the fact that they have salient visual properties of repetitiveness and symmetry.

It would be wrong to imagine that because symmetry and repetition are mathematical properties of forms, that it is not these properties which most readily provoke the illusion-if it is only that-of immanent causality in the index. Nothing could be more animated than the tessellations (tiling patterns) devised by Islamic decorative artisans and book illuminators. The religiously imposed ban on the representation of living forms only served, it seems, to inspire ever more effective inducements to captivation by visual artifice, the non-mimetic appearance of animation.

zh: 6.4　对称与生命感的显现
en: 6.4　Symmetry and the Appearance of Animation

zh: 数学关系如何以这种方式引发生命感？纹样形式的实际数学基础在概念上不难把握，尽管应用起来较难。所有纹样都不过是重复母题所能经受的四种“平面刚性运动”的变体。即（1）反射，（2）平移，（3）旋转，（4）滑移反射。这四种运动在[
]中展示并解释。最简单的装饰纹样类型是[
]所示的一维带状纹样。这种纹样（希腊回纹）由单一母题沿一条线的连续“平移”构成。它似乎在运动，因为我们像读一行文字那样“读”它，把注意力从一个母题移到另一个母题；为了观察它的对称性、从而它的纹样性，我们必须这样做。“看见”这一纹样的过程，就是辨认出母题 A 与 B、C、D 等相同，而且位于它们左侧。

由于感知这一纹样的过程涉及在心理上把母题向右平移，以便使母题与相邻母题重叠，从而认出它们彼此吻合，能动性与运动似乎就内在于母题本身。把感知所涉及的能动性（感知行为）投射或外化到被感知之物中，从认知上说，正是其生命感的来源。把纹样内在的生命感描述为幻觉、仿佛它是某种错误，是无益的。把太阳描述为“穿过”天空“运动”并不涉及错误。实际上，运动的是观察者而不是太阳，但太阳的运动并不像梦那样是纯主观现象。同样，我们并不是梦见纹样中的构成母题在运动，因为这些运动最终源于我们身体和感知器官扫描环境时的真实运动。
en: How do mathematical relations induce animacy in this way? The actual mathematical basis of patterned forms is not hard to grasp conceptually, though it is more difficult to apply. All patterns are variations on only four 'rigid motions in the plane', to which repeated motifs can be subjected. These are, (1) reflection, (2) translation, (3) rotation, and (4) glide reflection. These four motions are shown and explained in
. The simplest type of decorative pattern is the one-dimensional band pattern of the type shown in

. This pattern (a Greek key) consists of the successive 'translations' of a single motif along a line. It seems to move, because we 'read' it as we would a line of text, by moving our attention from motif to motif, which we must do, in order to observe its symmetry, and hence its patterned-ness. The process of 'seeing' this pattern is a matter of registering the fact that motif A is identical to, and to the left of, B, and C and D, and so on.

Because the process of perceiving this pattern involves mentally translating the motif to the right, so as to lay the motif down on its neighbour and register the congruence between them, agency and motion seems to inhere in the motifs themselves. The projection, or externalization, of the agency involved in perception (the perceptual act) into the thing perceived is, cognitively speaking, the source of its animation. It is unhelpful to describe the animation inherent in patterns as an illusion, as if it were some species of mistake. There is no mistake involved in describing the sun as ‘moving' through the sky. Actually, it is the observer who is moving, not the sun, but the sun's movement is not a purely subjective phenomenon, like a dream. Similarly, we do not dream that the constituent motifs in patterns move, because these movements stem ultimately from the real movements of our bodies and perceptual organs, scanning the environment.

zh: 关于似动与似因果的心理实验（如米肖特的著名实验）揭示了人类受试者多么容易把运动和相互因果互动归于最简陋的刺激。然而，即便人们能为纹样形式的生命外观提供一种认知解释——作为一种似动现象，知觉行为的动态方面被主观地体验为被感知对象的动态属性——那仍然解释不了为什么纹样性是人工制品如此普遍的属性，尤其是衣服、器皿等个人财产和用具。要理解这一点，必须考虑更复杂、更现实的例子。最重要的是，有纹样的物件和用具不是用“简单”纹样装饰的，而是用微妙而复杂的纹样，往往包含同时在平面两个维度上排列的许多母题，并涉及比简单平移更奥涩的平面运动。纯粹的复杂性、套叠，以及同时暗示母题之间大量形式关系，是一般装饰艺术的特征。人们不能从简单、易于解释的例子概括出对装饰艺术的理解，因为装饰艺术的目的朝向相反的方向：朝向复杂、歧义与繁多。
en: Psychological experiments on apparent motion and apparent causality (such as the famous experiments of Michotte) reveal how ready human subjects are to attribute motion and mutual causal interaction to the barest of stimuli. Nevertheless, even if one can provide a cognitive explanation for the animated appearance of patterned forms-as a phenomenon of apparent motion whereby the dynamic aspect of the act of perception is subjectively experienced as a dynamic property of the object being perceived-that still does not explain why patterned-ness is such a common property of artefacts, especially objects which are personal possessions and utensils, such as clothes, vessels, and so on. In order to understand this, one has to consider rather more complicated and realistic examples. Most significantly patterned objects and utensils are not decorated with ‘simple' patterns, but with subtle and complicated ones, often comprising a great many motifs deployed in two dimensions simultaneously, and involving more recondite motions in the plane than simple translation. Sheer complexity, involution, and the simultaneous suggestion of a great many formal relationships between motifs is a characteristic of decorative art in general. One cannot understand decorative art by generalizing from simple, easily interpreted, examples, because the telos of decorative art lies in the opposite direction, towards the complex, the ambiguous, and the multitudinous.

zh: 复杂纹样处于视觉“纹理”与“形状”的边界上。吉布森在其对自然情境（或称“生态”情境）下视觉知觉的说明里，对纹理的知觉与形状的知觉作了尖锐区分：纹理是有结构的表面（天空、绿色草坪、砖墙），形状则是球、杆、杯等。纹理被知觉为由组件（白与蓝的斑块、草叶、单块砖等）层级构成，但这些组件不被单独挑出；它们不是作为对象、而是作为表面的组件被关注。我们可以把纹样当作未区分内部形状的纹理来感知，而且经常如此，但当我们作为纹样来关注它们时则不然。然而，当我们这样做时，也不能完全把它们抽象为“形状”；它们保留着内在层级、划分为母题、母题块与模糊边缘这一本质的“纹理”特征。
en: Complicated patterns lie on the borderline between visual ‘textures' and ‘shapes'. Gibson, in his account of visual perception in naturalistic (or 'ecological' contexts), makes a sharp distinction between the perception of textures, which are structured surfaces (the sky, a green lawn, a brick wall) and the perception of shapes (a ball, a rod, a cup, etc.). Textures are perceived hierarchically constituted out of components (patches of white and blue, blades of grass, individual bricks, etc.) but these are not picked out individually; they are not attended to as objects but as components of a surface. We can respond to patterns as undifferentiated textures, and often do, but not when we attend to them as patterns. However, when we do this, we cannot entirely abstract them as ‘shapes' either; they retain their essential ‘texture' characteristic of internal hierarchy, division into motifs, blocs of motifs, and vague fringes.

en: In practice (and without the assistance of Washburn and Crowe), I think what happens is approximately as follows; what we do is single out, initially, a candidate motif, approximately, the axe-like shape (cf.

) which we spontaneously see as being repeated (by translation) in rows and columns, and we may also be dimly aware that the ‘ground' on which this shape is laid has the same shapes inscribed on it, but in reverse colour. What, however, is likely to defeat us is seeing the relation between the figure and the ground, and the relation of the leftwards-pointing and rightwards-pointing occurrences of our candidate ‘basic' motif. So in fact we just mentally resign ourselves to just not quite understanding these complex relationships, we write them in as ‘beyond our ken'. We experience this as a kind of pleasurable frustration; we are drawn into the pattern and held inside it, impaled, as it were, on its bristling hooks and spines. This pattern is a mind-trap (cf. Gell 1996), we are hooked, and this causes us to relate in a certain way to the artefact which the pattern embellishes.

zh: 6.6　作为“未竟之事”的复杂纹样
en: 6.6　Complex Patterns as Unfinished Business

zh: 纹样凭借其繁多性，以及我们仅凭视觉检查难以把握其数学或几何基础这一点，在时间中生成人与物之间的关系，因为它们呈现给心智的，从认知上说，永远是“未竟之事”。拥有一块繁复东方地毯的人，谁能说自己已完全把握了它的纹样；然而眼睛又多么频繁地停留在它上面，时而挑出这一关系、这一对称，时而挑出那一关系、那一对称。这一过程可以无休止地继续；纹样是不可穷尽的，地毯与所有者的关系则是终生的。人类学家早已认识到，社会关系要经久持续，就必须建立在“未竟之事”上。交换作为一种维系关系的社会力量的本质，在于交易之间的延迟或滞后；如果交换关系要持续，就绝不应导致完全的互惠，而总是导致某种每次都会重新出现的余留不平衡。纹样也是如此；它们放慢知觉，甚至使其停摆，以至于装饰过的对象从未被完全占有，而总是处于正在被占有的过程中。我认为，这在装饰索引与接受者之间建立了一种贯穿个人生命史的关系，也就是一场未完成的交换。
en: Patterns, by their multiplicity and the difficulty we have in grasping their mathematical or geometrical basis by mere visual inspection, generate relationships over time between persons and things, because what they present to the mind is, cognitively speaking, always ‘unfinished business'. Who, possessed of an intricate oriental carpet, can say that they have entirely come to grips with its pattern; yet how often the eye rests on it and singles out now this relation, this symmetry, now that. The process can continue interminably; the pattern is inexhaustible, the relationship between carpet and owner, for life. Anthropologists have long recognized that social relationships, to endure over time, have to be founded on ‘unfinished business'. The essence of exchange, as a binding social force, is the delay, or lag, between transactions which, if the exchange relation is to endure, should never result in perfect reciprocation, but always in some renewed, residual, imbalance. So it is with patterns; they slow perception down, or even halt it, so that the decorated object is never fully possessed at all, but is always in the process of becoming possessed. This, I argue, sets up a biographical relation-an unfinished exchange-between the decorated index and the recipient.

zh: 6.7　品味与俗气
en: 6.7　Taste and Tackiness

zh: 有人可能会反驳说，上一节的论证偏离了要点。装饰过的对象之所以使人愉悦，是因为它们提供审美快乐，这才是它们令人向往的原因，而不是像我声称的那样因为它们在认知上抗拒分析。人们就是“喜欢”漂亮的纹样。对这一反驳，我要回答：第一，并非每个人都喜欢漂亮（复杂、有生命感等）的纹样；第二，单纯的审美“喜欢”解释不了由纹样人工制品中介的社会关系类型。
en: It could be objected that the argument of the preceding section is beside the point. Decorated objects please people because they confer aesthetic pleasure, and that is why they are desirable, not because they are cognitively resistant to analysis, as I have claimed. People just ‘like' pretty patterns. To this objection I would answer that, first, not everybody does like pretty (complicated, animated, etc.) patterns, and secondly that mere aesthetic ‘liking' cannot explain the types of social relationships which are mediated by patterned artefacts.

zh: 审美愉悦本身就是终点，是自足的目的，可是并无经验证据表明人们会脱离具体情境去观赏随处可见的装饰物。在那些情境里，审美属性从来不是唯一受到关注的方面。美拉尼西亚的大人物不会围坐着审美地沉思石灰罐；相反，他们把石灰罐当作中介对象来对待。石灰罐不是自足的快乐源泉，而是人格的载体，供人占有、交换和展示。艺术的美学理论意味着，任何两个艺术品的接受者，只要审美趣味相同（这尤其适用于两个美拉尼西亚大人物），就会对任何给定对象的审美属性作出相同反应。但实践中从来不是这样；就这些大人物而言，索引（如石灰罐）中呈现的内在品质，是被葫芦所有者的身份与地位所调节的。石灰罐的审美属性只有在它们于社会场域中往复传递社会能动性时才变得显著。
en: Aesthetic pleasure is consummatory, an end in itself, and there is nothing empirically to show that the decorated objects with which the world abounds are contemplated except in specific situational contexts in which their aesthetic properties are never the sole focus of interest. Melanesian big-men do not sit around aesthetically contemplating lime-containers; on the contrary, they treat them as mediating objects. Lime-containers are not self-sufficient sources of delight, but vehicles of personhood, to be owned, exchanged, and displayed. Aesthetic theories of art imply that any two recipients of an artwork, if they have the same aesthetic tastes (which would apply, afortiori, to two Melanesian big-men) will have the same response to the aesthetic properties of any given object. But this is never the case in practice; so far as these big-men are concerned, the inherent quality present in an index (such as a lime-container) is modulated by the identity and status of the gourd's owner. The aesthetic properties of a lime-container are salient only to the extent that they mediate social agency back and forth within the social field.

zh: 同样，我要否认：沉思一块自己不拥有的东方地毯，与沉思一块自己私有的地毯，是同一种体验。正如亨利·詹姆斯那篇著名小说所写，复杂东方设计地毯的拥有者，在其盘绕中看到的是自己未竟一生的意象。别人的地毯则完全不然，它只是不可实现之欲望的罗网。美学家们无疑会对这类情感的表达感到惊骇，但从人类学上看，再明显不过的是：审美反应从属于由索引中介的社会身份与差异所产生的反应。既然纯粹审美反应是一个神话，就不能援引它来解释人与物之间多种多样的附着类型。审美反应总是发生在某种社会框架之内。
en: Similarly, I would deny that the contemplation of an oriental carpet that one does not own is the same kind of experience as the contemplation of a carpet that is one's personal possession. The possessor of a carpet of complicated oriental design, as in the well-known Henry James story, sees in its coils an image of his own unfinished life. It is quite otherwise with somebody else's carpet, which is just a snare for unrealizable desire. Aestheticians will no doubt be horrified at the expression of such sentiments, but anthropologically, it is abundantly obvious that aesthetic responses are subordinate to responses stemming from the social identities and differences mediated by the index. Since the pure aesthetic response is a myth, it cannot be invoked to explain the very manifold types of attachment between persons and things. The aesthetic response always occurs within a social frame of some kind.

zh: 其次，就特有的西方（乃至东方）“审美态度”而言，往往激起最肆意赞赏的，恰恰是缺乏我所关注的那种繁复表面装饰的对象。按照精致的品味准则，简单而无装饰的形式是最美的；同样，在宗教态度倾向于禁欲与退隐的人看来也是如此。正如 E. 贡布里希（1984）所示，最坚定的唯美主义者远非热衷于恣肆的装饰；然而装饰即使面对来自上层的审美谴责，依然存活并繁荣，因为它在社会上有效力。我个人，作为品味精致者的化身，甚至过度地赞赏极简的震教徒家具；但从人类学上，我知道这种家具产生于一个共同体，该共同体出于神学理由，明确禁止了装饰对象在较少清教色彩的社会环境中所允许的那类中介。震教徒的椅子做得朴素，是为了让震教徒不附着于椅子或其他尘世之物，而只附着于主耶稣。上层资产阶级的康德式美学解释不了装饰，因为康德式美学是反对装饰的。
en: Secondly, when it comes to the specifically Western (or, indeed, Oriental) ‘aesthetic attitude' it is objects devoid of precisely the kind of intricate surface decoration of the type I am interested in that have often excited the most extravagant admiration. Simple and undecorated forms are the most beautiful according to refined canons of taste, and equally, to those whose religious attitudes incline them towards asceticism and withdrawal. As E. Gombrich (1984) has shown, most committed aesthetes are far from keen on riotous decoration, which, however, survives and prospers, even in the face of aesthetic condemnation from on high, because it is socially efficacious. I, personally, in my incarnation as a person of refined tastes, admire even to excess ultra-plain Shaker furniture, but anthropologically, I know that this furniture came into existence in a community which specifically, on theological grounds, outlawed the kinds of mediation which decorated objects allow in less puritanical social milieux. Shaker chairs were made plain so that Shakers would not be attached to chairs, or other earthly things, but exclusively to Lord Jesus. Kantian high-bourgeois aesthetics cannot explain decoration because Kantian aesthetics is against decoration.

zh: 大多数人不像震教徒，他们更喜欢在表面堆满装饰，以便把人吸引到世俗生活的种种事务中。一把华丽的维多利亚式椅子远不如震教徒椅子美，但它传达得强烈得多：不只是舒适地坐着的观念，还有许多关乎尘世生活的家庭与社会意涵。
en: Most people are not like Shakers, they prefer to load surfaces with decoration in order to draw persons into worldly projects. An ornate Victorian chair is not half so beautiful as a Shaker one, but it communicates much more strongly, not just the idea of sitting comfortably, but also a host of other domestic and social implications of a this-worldly variety.

zh: 贡布里希（1984: 17-32）追溯了赞成与反对装饰的风尚如何在欧洲品味史上蔓延。清教运动，如阿道夫·路斯所表述的革命性现代主义，鄙视表面装饰；而浪漫的享乐主义者，如用花朵和星星定制自己大众汽车的1960年代嬉皮士，则热爱它。我不打算重述贡布里希出色的历史；相反，我要把注意力集中在我所认定的表面装饰的本质属性上：它的认知抗拒，即一旦屈从于纹样的诱惑，就容易上钩、被困于其中。
en: Gombrich (1984: 17-32) has traced the epidemiology of pro- and antidecoration sentiment in the history of European taste. Puritan movements, such as the revolutionary modernism articulated by Adolf Loos, despise surface ornamentation, while romantic hedonists such as the 1960s hippies who customized their Volkswagens with flowers and stars, adore it. I am not going to recapitulate Gombrich's excellent history; instead I want to focus attention on what I have identified as the essential property of surface decoration, its cognitive resistance, the fact that once one submits to the allure of the pattern, one is liable to become hooked, or stuck, in it.

zh: 严峻的现代主义从一系列可能的词中选中“俗气”（tacky）
一词，来谴责大众对恣肆装饰及其他品味失误的喜好，这一事实本身就很有趣。让我引用玛丽·道格拉斯对萨特关于“黏滞性”作为一种卑贱存在状态的说明的概述（Douglas 1966: 38; Sartre 1943: 696 ff.）：
en: The fact that the word ‘tacky' is the one selected (from a range of possibilities) by severe modernism to condemn the popular taste for riotous ornament and other lapses of taste is interesting in itself. Let me quote from Mary Douglas's summary of Sartre's account of ‘viscosity' as an ignoble state of being (Douglas 1966: 38; Sartre 1943: 696 ff.):

zh: 黏滞是介于固体与液体之间的中间状态。它像是变化过程中的一个横截面。它不稳定，但也不流动。它柔软，受力容易变形，也可以压缩。它的表面无法滑过。它的黏性是一个陷阱，它像水蛭一样附着；它攻击我与它之间的边界。从我指间垂落的长条黏液暗示我自身的实体流入一摊黏滞之中……触碰黏滞就是冒着把我自身稀释为黏滞的风险……
en: The viscous is a state half-way between solid and liquid. It is like a cross-section in a process of change. It is unstable, but it does not flow. It is soft, yielding and compressible. There is no gliding on its surface. Its stickiness is a trap, it clings like a leech; it attacks the boundary between myself and it. Long columns falling off my fingers suggest my own substance flowing into a pool of stickiness ... to touch stickiness is to risk diluting myself into viscosity ...

zh: 萨特对黏滞性对身体／世界边界的颠覆效果感到不安，但鉴于后莫斯式的理解——礼物是人的黏性组件，串在赠与者和接受者之间、由黏滞（即便是想象的）物质构成的环上——我们不必对这种感觉如此反感。物理／触觉的黏着也许确实令人不快，但类比的或认知的黏着则不然，否则我们就不会如此乐意让人工制品附着于我们，如此积极地回应表面装饰的黏着品质。大多数非现代主义、非清教的文明都重视装饰性，并赋予它在社会生活中介、在人与物之间创造附着方面的特定角色。
en: Sartre is perturbed by the subversive effect of viscosity on the body/world boundary, but in the light of post-Maussian understandings of gifts as adhesive components of persons, strung between donors and recipients on loops of viscous (if imaginary) substance, we need not be so squeamish. Physical/tactile adhesiveness is perhaps genuinely disagreeable, but analogical, or cognitive, adhesiveness is not, otherwise we would not be so willing to have artefacts attached to us and so positively responsive to the adhesive qualities of surface decoration. Most non-modernist, non-puritan civilizations value decorativeness and allot it a specific role in the mediation of social life, the creation of attachment between persons and things.

en: 6.8　The Apotropaic Pattern

zh: 指的是索引本质上的层级性质，即它由组合成整体的各部分构成（这适用于所有索引，但在此语境中尤为显著）。我的论点是：对这一层级关系复合体的解构，赋予装饰对象某种类型的能动性，它是接受者在（试图）感知它时所行使的能动性的对应物；他的行动被主观地体验为一种受动、一种令人愉悦的挫败。然而，其他类型的能动性也可能在场。特别是，艺术家的能动性可以从纹样中溯因得出。因此公式可以轻松扩展为：
en: refers to the essentially hierarchical nature of the index, the fact that it is composed of parts combined into a whole (this applies to all indexes, but is particularly salient in this context). My argument is that the deconstruction of this complex of hierarchical relationships endows the decorated object with a certain type of agency, which is the reciprocal of the agency exercised by the recipient in (attempting) to perceive it; his action is subjectively experienced as a passion, a pleasurable frustration. However, other types of agency may be present as well. In particular, the agency of the artist may be abducted from the pattern. Thus the formula can easily be expanded to:

zh: 这种能动性可以是对抗性的或防御性的，也可以是有益性的。我现在转向一系列例子，其中社会能动性的行使取决于把纹样用作主动敌意或防御意图的中介。纹样把人与物联结起来，却可能在冲突情境中成为潜在武器，这似乎悖谬。稍加反思就足以认识到：首先，冲突与斗争的关系和团结的关系一样是“社会性的”；其次，凡有冲突之处，就能发现各种装饰艺术的大量部署。这类艺术大多属于所谓“辟邪”品种。辟邪艺术保护施动者（我们暂且认定为艺术家）免受接受者（通常是以恶魔而非人形出现的敌人）之害，是艺术能动性的首要实例，因而也是艺术人类学核心关注的主题。
en: This agency can be agonistic or defensive as well as beneficial. I turn now to a series of examples in which the exercise of social agency turns on the employment of patterns as mediators of actively hostile, or defensive, intent. It might seem paradoxical that patterns, which bind persons to things, should be potential weapons in situations of conflict. A moment's reflection is sufficient to realize, first of all, that relations of conflict and struggle are just as ‘social' as relations of solidarity, and secondly, that wherever one finds conflict there one finds abundant deployment of all kinds of decorative art. Much of this art is of the variety known as ‘apotropaic'. Apotropaic art, which protects an agent (whom we will take to be the artist, for the present) against the recipient (usually the enemy in demonic rather than human form), is a prime instance of artistic agency, and hence a topic of central concern in the anthropology of art.

zh: 纹样的辟邪用途是作为保护装置、防御屏障或阻碍通行的障碍物。纹样的这种“辟邪”用途似乎悖谬，因为放置纹样以驱避恶魔，似乎与纹样在其他语境中用作促成人与人工制品之间附着的手段相反。如果纹样有吸引力，难道它们不会也吸引而非驱避恶魔吗？但这一悖谬只是表面而非真实的，因为纹样的辟邪用途与用纹样吸引人于物的用途一样，都依赖于黏着性。辟邪纹样实际上是恶魔陷阱，仿佛专黏恶魔的捕蝇纸，恶魔一旦黏住就再也脱不了身，也就不能作害。
en: The apotropaic use of patterns is as protective devices, defensive screens or obstacles impeding passage. This 'apotropaic' use of patterns seems paradoxical in that the placing of patterns to keep demons at bay seems contrary to the use of patterns in other contexts as a means of bringing about attachment between people and artefacts. If patterns attract, wouldn't they also attract, rather than repel demons? But the paradox is apparent rather than real in that the apotropaic use of patterns depends on adhesiveness just as the use of patterns to attract people to things. Apotropaic patterns are demon-traps, in effect, demonic fly-paper, in which demons become hopelessly stuck, and are thus rendered harmless.

zh: 以[

]中的凯尔特结绳纹为例。这类结绳纹被视为具有保护性，因为任何恶灵都会被缠绕的辫纹迷住，以致意志瘫痪。恶魔对它先前怀有的任何恶意计划失去兴趣，被困在纹样的盘绕之中，而受其保护的对象、人或地点就得救了。不只是繁复的纹样，纯粹的繁多也能产生这种效果；有人告诉我，甚至在不久前的意大利，农民还会在床架旁挂一小袋谷物，这样魔鬼接近床上睡眠者时，就不得不数袋中的谷粒，于是分了神，顾不上加害。数不过来的大数量与复杂纹样以同样的方式起作用；但纹样更有趣，也无疑更艺术。
en: Take the Celtic knotwork pattern in

. Knotwork like this was regarded as protective in that any evil spirit would be so fascinated by the entwined braids as to suffer from a paralysis of the will. Losing interest in whatever malevolent plan it had entertained previously, the demon would become stuck in the coils of the pattern and the object, person, or place protected by it would be saved. Not just intricate pattern, but sheer multiplicity can have this effect; I am told that even recently in Italy, peasants would hang a little bag of grain next to the bedstead, so that the Devil, approaching the sleeper in the bed, would be obliged to count the grains in the bag and would be thus diverted from inflicting harm. The interminableness of large numbers and complicated patterns work in the same way; but patterns are more interesting and certainly more artistic.

zh: 6.9　科拉姆
en: 6.9　Kolam

zh: 一个合适的例子是泰米尔纳德（南印度）称为科拉姆的那类吉祥门槛图纹；在印度南部和东部其他也绘制类似门槛图纹的地区，它另有名称[

]。在泰米尔纳德，科拉姆有两种保护功能。首先，它们与保护性的、丰产的、吉祥的眼镜蛇神（那伽）相联系；其次，它们有辟邪功能，驱避或诱捕恶魔。科拉姆由妇女制作，她们用石灰、米粉或其他白色粉末徒手绘制图纹，粉末从指间洒落。图纹在黎明时分制作，尤其是在一年中恶魔与精灵出没较多的时节，随着白天脚步的往来而被磨掉，次日再重新绘制（Layard 1937: 121，引 J. Dubois 与 S. M. N. Sastri）。[
]展示了一个典型的科拉姆设计。科拉姆是蜿蜒、对称的图形，通常很难“读”——即很难看出图纹是如何构造的。它们与观者玩拓扑游戏，因此类似于迷宫。让我们把[
]拆开，看看这里在进行什么样的认知挑逗。
en: A suitable example is provided by the kind of auspicious threshold designs known in Tamilnad (South India) as kolam, and by other names in other parts of southern and eastern India where similar threshold designs are also drawn (

). In Tamilnad, kolam have two protective functions. First of all they are associated with the protective, fertile, and auspicious cobra deity (naga) and secondly they have an apotropaic function, repelling or ensnaring demons. Kolam are made by women, who draw the design free-hand in lime, rice-powder, or some other white powder which they trickle through their fingers. The designs are made at dawn, especially during the time of year when there are many demons and spirits about, and are rubbed out by the passage of feet as the day wears on, to be renewed the next day (Layard 1937: 121, citing J. Dubois, and S. M. N. Sastri).

shows a typical kolam design. Kolam are sinuous, symmetrical figures which are usually very difficult to ‘read' in the sense that it is difficult to see how the design has been constructed. They play topological games with the spectator and are thus akin to mazes. Let us take
apart and see what kind of cognitive teasing is going on here.

en: FIG. 6.9/1. Kolam threshold design: the pattern as topological snare

zh: 乍看之下，它似乎由一条单线构成，在点阵的行与列之间走一条复杂、蜿蜒的路径。然而这是一种幻觉，因为这个科拉姆实际上由四个不对称构形的连续环组成，每个环相对前一个环旋转90度，再把四个环叠合。可以说，这个科拉姆是四声部卡农的视觉对应物：每个声部唱相同的音符，进入的时间却彼此错开，就像《雅克兄弟》（Frère Jacques）那样滞后一小节。它的相同组件（各个环）也彼此错开，只是错位发生在空间中，每次旋转90度（[
en: On first inspection, it seems to consist of a single line, pursuing a complex, sinuous path between the rows and columns of dots. However, this is an illusion in that this kolam is actually composed of four continuous loops of asymmetric configuration, superimposed on one another while being rotated in 90 degree steps. This kolam is, so to speak, the visual equivalent of a canon in four parts, in which each voice sings the same notes but not in phase; that is, after the lapse of one bar as in ‘Frere Jacques'. The identical components (individual loops) of this are out of phase, not in time, but in space, being displaced by 90 degree rotations (

zh: 这个科拉姆最有趣之处在于：即便一个人（在理智上）“知道”这个设计由四个独立但相同、取向不同的环组成，试图从整体设计中抽象出单个环也极其令人挫败。我发现，费些力气我可以一次对一个环做到这一点，但无法同时对两个环做到，更不用说三个或全部四个。就简单几何图形而言，“看见”（比如一个三角形）等同于在头脑中逐线预想或模拟这一图形的构造。但对科拉姆这样的复杂图形，这不可能做到。在这里，看见图形与能够在头脑中预想它的构造过程是完全不同的两回事。然而我们仍在心里“补上”了这一事实：这个图形可以被构造出来，因为它就在这里，是某人做出来的，而且我们也许确实有幸着迷地观看过制作它的妇女的灵巧动作。于是我们以一系列悖论告终。我们想把这个图形看作一条连续线，但我们知道它是四个独立的环，却又无法把它们从整体设计中分别抽象出来。我们也知道这个设计属于现实世界，是这位真实妇女显然毫不费力地做出来的；但我们无法完全重溯该设计经由这位妇女的能动性进入世界的过程，因为我们无法从作为其结果的设计中重构她的熟练动作（以及指导这些动作的意图）。
en: What is most interesting about this kolam is that even if one ‘knows' (intellectually) that this design is made up of four separate, but identical loops differently orientated, it is extremely frustrating to attempt to abstract individual loops from the overall design. And though I find I can, with some effort, do this for one loop at a time, I cannot do it for two loops simultaneously, still less three, or all four. Where simple geometric figures are concerned, ‘seeing' (a triangle, say) is tantamount to mentally intending or projecting the construction of the figure, line by line. But this is impossible to do with complex figures like this kolam. Here seeing the figure is quite distinct from being able to mentally intend the process of its construction. Yet we ‘write in' the fact that it is possible to construct the figure, because here it is, it has been made by someone, and we might indeed have been lucky enough to have watched, entranced, the deft movements of the woman who made it. So we end with a series of paradoxes. We want to see this figure as one continuous line, but we know it is four separate loops, which, however, we cannot separately abstract from the overall design. We know too that this design belongs to the real world, and was made, apparently effortlessly, by this real woman; but we cannot retrace fully the process whereby the design came into the world, by the agency of this woman, because we cannot reconstruct her skilled movements (and the intentions guiding them) from the design which has resulted from them.

zh: 我把纹样的认知黏性归因于重构人工制品所体现的意向性这一认知过程中的阻塞。显然，没有恶魔会轻易跨过设有如此精巧拓扑罗网的门槛；恶者不得不暂停下来琢磨这个问题，这股想要作害的劲头便被消解了。也许并非巧合：妇女们玩这些数学游戏的泰米尔纳德邦，也正是印度大多数世界闻名的数学家和计算机奇才的出身之邦。
en: I attribute the cognitive stickiness of patterns to this blockage in the cognitive process of reconstructing the intentionality embodied in artefacts. Clearly, no demon will readily cross a threshold set with sophisticated topological snares such as this; the evil one will have to pause and ponder the problem, and the impetus of its malevolence will be neutralized. Perhaps it is no coincidence that Tamilnad, the state where women play these mathematical games, is also the state from which most of India's world-renowned mathematicians and computer wizards originate.

zh: 6.10　科拉姆、纹身与克里特迷宫
en: 6.10　Kolam, Tattoo, and the Cretan Maze

zh: 在20世纪早期，与科拉姆经常完全相同的图纹另有用途——作为纹身图纹，守卫的不是房屋的门槛，而是皮肤，即身体的门槛。这为我论证的下一阶段——与迷宫有关——提供了衔接。取自 Layard 1937 的[

]展示了20世纪初发表的一个南印度纹身图纹，并作为对照，展示了公元前7世纪克里特钱币上所绘的克诺索斯迷宫（即容纳弥诺陶洛斯的那个）的“地图”。传说中，这座迷宫由大师级工匠代达罗斯设计，并仿照另一座迷宫——通往冥界的那座——建造。《埃涅阿斯纪》第6卷提到克里特迷宫的类似表现，刻在库迈的大门上，吸引了埃涅阿斯随从的注意；随后他们的领袖下入冥界去求问库迈的西比尔，后者预言罗马有一天将统治世界。奇怪的是，在爱尔兰纽格莱奇大通道墓的入口旁，也刻着一幅完全相同的迷宫地图，而那条墓道确实也是一条蜿蜒的隧道，想必通往死者的世界。古埃及艺术中也有位于迷宫中心的神祇表现。
en: In the earlier part of this century, designs frequently identical to kolam had an alternative use as tattoo designs, defending not the threshold of the house, but the skin, the threshold of the body. And this provides a link with the next stage of my argument, which has to do with mazes.

taken from Layard 1937, shows a South Indian tattoo design published at the beginning of this century, and for comparison, a ‘map' of the labyrinth at Knossos (the one containing the Minotaur) as depicted on a Cretan coin of the seventh century BC. Legendarily, this labyrinth was designed by the master-craftsman Daedalus, and was modelled on another maze, the one which led to the Underworld. A similar representation of the Cretan labyrinth is mentioned in book 6 of the Aeneid, as being carved on the Cumaean gates, where it attracts the attention of Aeneas' men, prior to their leader's descent into the Underworld to consult the Cumaean Sibyl, who predicts that one day Rome will rule the world. Curiously, an exactly identical map of the labyrinth is to be found carved next to the entry into the great passage-grave at New Grange, in Ireland, which is indeed also a twisting tunnel leading, presumably, to the world of the dead. There are also representations of gods at the centre of labyrinths in the art of ancient Egypt.

zh: 我为什么提到这些曾使人类学家莱亚德和他那个时代的古典学者如此兴奋的事实？莱亚德如今是人类学中被遗忘的人物，他对这类事情的兴趣，在一个由拉德克利夫-布朗和马林诺夫斯基的功能主义主导的时代，注定了他声誉的衰落。莱亚德是心理学取向的那批传播论者中的最后一人，这批人的理论框架取自里弗斯；如今唯一仍在印行的莱亚德著作，是他后来作为荣格派分析学家所写的那些，据说可以在“神秘学”书店找到。鉴于刚才提到的事实，人们可以理解莱亚德为何放弃学院人类学，成为荣格“原型”的倡导者。相同的迷宫纹样竟在南印度、古代地中海、埃及和爱尔兰的泥沼中被发掘出来，确实令人惊讶；尤其因为我们将会看到，莱亚德在太平洋中央的新赫布里底（瓦努阿图）也发现了把“迷宫”图纹与进入死者之地联系起来的类似观念。我对莱亚德抱有同情，因为在某种意义上，他是被手头材料彼此吻合这一点本身“逼”去追求一种（在当时）极不合潮流的传播论进路的，而这些数据除了里弗斯式或荣格式的解释之外，确实似乎没有别的明显解释。
en: Why do I mention these facts, which so excited the anthropologist Layard and the classical scholars of his period? Layard is now a forgotten figure in anthropology, and his interest in matters such as these ensured the demise of his reputation in an era dominated by the functionalism of Radcliffe-Brown and Malinowski. Layard was the last of the diffusionists of a psychological persuasion, who drew their theoretical framework from Rivers, and nowadays the only Layard works in print are those he wrote later on as a Jungian analyst, which are to be found, I am told, in ‘Occult' bookstores. One can see why Layard abandoned academic anthropology and became a proponent of Jungian ‘archetypes' in the light of the facts just mentioned. It is indeed astonishing that identical maze-patterns should be unearthed in South India, the ancient Mediterranean, Egypt, and the bogs of Ireland, especially so in that, as we will see, Layard found similar ideas linking ‘maze' designs and entry into the land of the dead also in the New Hebrides (Vanuatu) in the midst of the Pacific ocean. I feel sympathy for Layard in that he was in a sense ‘bounced' into pursuing a deeply untrendy diffusionist approach (for the time) by the sheer coherence of the data at his disposal, for which there does indeed appear no obvious explanation other than a Riversian or Jungian one.

zh: 我个人看不出为什么应该不假思索地摒弃传播论解释（参列维-斯特劳斯 1963）。但我想在这里讨论的不是传播论假说。即便“克里特迷宫”观念是从某个特定起源地传播到全球的，人们仍然必须解释为何差异极大的文明会格外容易接受这一观念，且需要比荣格诉诸古代种族记忆的存留更有说服力的解释。至于迷宫观念究竟如何存在于这么多不同地方、而且显然都与现世和死者之地之间的通道相联系，人们可以存而不论。我关心的问题是理解这一迷宫纹样的认知意义，它能同样好地解释为什么它传播得如此广远，和／或为什么它在这么多相距遥远的地方被独立发明出来。
en: I personally do not see why one should dismiss diffusionist explanations out of hand (cf. Levi-Strauss 1963). But it is not the diffusionist hypothesis that I want to discuss here. Even if the ‘Cretan maze' idea has spread across the globe from some specific place of origin, one would still have to explain the enhanced receptivity of very diverse civilizations to this idea, on a better basis than the preservation of ancient racial memories, as Jung proposes. One can afford to be agnostic about how exactly the labyrinth idea came to exist in so many different places with apparently the same associations, having to do with the passage between this world and the land of the dead. The problem I am concerned with is to understand the cognitive significance of this maze-pattern, which could equally well explain why it has travelled so far and wide and/or why it has been invented independently in so many mutually faraway places.

zh: 严格说来，克里特迷宫不是“迷宫”（maze），因为它没有分支通道，因而不构成导航问题。如果迷宫像[

]所示那样建造，忒修斯进出迷宫其实不需要阿里阿德涅的线。它是一种“回纹”（meander）纹样，是在两个空间上相当邻近的点之间寻找最长可能路径的一次尝试。它唤起导航问题的观念，却并不真正提供这样一个问题；毋宁说，问题是距离与连续统的问题。人们可以把克里特迷宫看作芝诺时间与运动悖论的空间版本。例如，芝诺论证说，飞行中的箭必须相继到达并越过无限多个点，即二分之一点、四分之三点、6/8点、12/16点、24/32点
等等，而由于这一分数序列是无限的，箭永远到达不了目的地。克里特迷宫通过串联各点（[
]）而建成，从而创造出一种回纹纹样，它有可能无限增加入口与中心之间必须经过的路径的转折次数。在罗马世界，回纹纹样（以及真正的迷宫纹样）是宫殿马赛克地面装饰的流行手段，其无限扩展有限空间的能力，在建筑上可能确实非常有效，同时也具有装饰性（见[
]，展示克罗地亚普拉的大迷宫）。这类迷宫例示了纹样呈现认知障碍的另一种方式。人们知道迷宫有路可通；人们甚至可能知道，迷宫是通过连接线与点的迭代规则的简单应用而创造的，如[
]所示；但尽管如此，人们还是无法看出穿越迷宫的路，除非极其费力地描出它蜿蜒的路线。
en: The Cretan labyrinth is not, technically, a ‘maze' in that it has no branching passageways and so poses no navigational problems. Theseus would not really have needed Ariadne's thread to find his way into or out of the labyrinth if it were built as shown in

. It is a ‘meander' pattern, an exercise in finding the longest possible pathway between two spatially quite adjacent points. It evokes the idea of a navigational problem without actually offering one, rather, the problem is one of distance and the continuum. One could see the Cretan maze as a spatial version of Zeno's paradoxes of time and motion. Zeno argued, for instance, that an arrow in its flight must successively reach, and pass, an infinite number of points, that is, the half-way point, the threequarters point, the 6/8 point, the 12/16 point, the 24/32 point, etc. etc. and that since this series of fractions is infinite, the arrow will never reach its destination. The Cretan maze is built up by connecting points serially (

) so as to create a meander pattern which threatens to indefinitely extend the number of twistings and turnings in the path which must be traversed between the entry-door and the centre. In the Roman world, meander patterns (and genuine maze-patterns) were a popular device for mosaic floor-decoration in palaces, where their capacity to expand confined spaces indefinitely may indeed have been architectonically highly effective, as well as decorative (see

, showing the great maze at Pula, in Croatia). Such mazes exemplify another way in which patterns can present cognitive obstacles. One knows there is a way through the maze; one may even know that the maze is created by the simple application of an iterative rule in connecting up lines and points, as is demonstrated in
, but one cannot, all the same, see one's way through the maze except very laboriously by tracing out its winding course.

zh: 这也许有助于解释为什么迷宫与生者世界和死者世界之间的通道相联系。这两个世界靠得很近（死亡无处不在），却又相距遥远，被一道不可逾越的边界隔开。埃涅阿斯的同伴被门上刻的迷宫纹样迷住了，未能进入库迈的大门；在这方面，他们类似于前面讨论的、被保护房屋的科拉姆拦住的恶魔。但科拉姆与迷宫图纹之间的联系比这更紧密，因为印度（基于科拉姆的）纹身图纹特别地与进入死者世界相联系。因此，[

]所示的纹身图纹除了在形式上与科拉姆相同之外，还属于印度纹身图纹中的一类，这类图纹出现于半岛的许多地区，被认定为死者之地的“堡垒”（即城市）。在整个印度，尤其在低种姓和部落中，妇女（有时还有男子）被认为必须纹身，以避免在死者之地受罚。“堡垒”图纹被认为能帮助死者（她死后仍保留纹身）找到通往死者之地的路，并安全地与已故亲人团聚。所以“堡垒”是一张地图。同时它也是一个谜，因为这同一批人相信，死神阎摩及其恶魔会吞食没有纹身的人，但不会伤害纹身妇女，因为他们解不开她的纹身所呈现的“谜”；也就是说，纹身在死后保护身体免遭邪祟（Gell n.d. [1994]）。因此科拉姆与“迷宫”纹身以同样的方式起作用——两者都代表这样一个观念：（恶魔的）注意力被纹样吸引、纠缠，恶魔由此受到阻拦，再无力作害。
en: This may help explain why mazes are associated with the passage between the worlds of the living and the dead. These worlds are close together (death is everywhere) yet far apart, separated by an impassable frontier. Aeneas' companions were prevented from entering the Cumaean gates by the fascination exerted over them by the maze design carved on the portal; in this respect they were akin to the demons waylaid by the kolam protecting the house, discussed earlier. But the connection between kolam and maze designs is closer than this, in that Indian (kolam-based) tattoo designs were specifically connected with entry into the world of the dead. Thus the tattoo design shown in

, besides being formally identical to a kolam, is one of the class of Indian tattoo designs, occurring in many regions of the peninsular, which are identified as the ‘fort' (i.e. City) of the land of the dead. Throughout India, especially among lower castes and tribes, it was considered a necessity for women, and sometimes men, to be tattooed, in order to avoid punishment in the land of the dead. The ‘fort' design was considered to help the dead person (who retained her tattoos post mortem) to find their way to the land of the dead and be safely reunited with deceased kin. So the ‘fort' is a map. At the same time, it is also a puzzle, in that these same people believe that Yama, the God of death, and his demons, will devour the untattooed, but will not harm the tattooed woman because they cannot solve the ‘puzzle' that her tattoos present, that is to say, the tattoo is apotropaically protective of the body after death (Gell n.d. [1994] ). So the kolam and the ‘maze' tattoo both work in the same way - both stand for the idea of (demonic) attention being drawn into the pattern, being tantalized by it, while being thus rebuffed and rendered impotent.

zh: 6.11　马拉库拉沙画与死者之地
en: 6.11　Sand-Drawings of Malakula and the Land of the Dead

zh: 纹样作为“障碍”——即黏着点——的观念，也出现在马拉库拉，即莱亚德及其年长同代人伯纳德·迪肯所研究的新赫布里底社会；迪肯在田野期间去世（迪肯和莱亚德都是里弗斯的学生）。马拉库拉人也许独一无二：他们对人类学文献的贡献不仅是作为民族志对象，而且是作为亲属理论中一种图示表现方法的创始者。一个马拉库拉男子为迪肯画的图（用长短木棍和沙上描出的弧线），展示马拉库拉以三类（或六类）划分的联姻制度的运作，显然是后来人类学家为澳大利亚同类制度制作图示的努力的先驱（Deacon 1934: [
]; Lévi-Strauss 1969: [
]）。马拉库拉人之所以这样擅长用图来思考，是因为他们把纹样构造作为一种艺术形式来实践，并作为典型的瓦努阿图男性以展示知识和技艺来争胜的活动的一部分。迪肯收集了四十五个以上图纹，在他去世后出版（[
]）。这些图纹由男子在海滩上绘制，当然会被涨潮冲掉。正如迪肯所指出的，马拉库拉沙画艺术中重要的不是生产出来的人工制品，而是程序的“表演”方面，即专家如何能毫不迟疑、毫不偏离地，以从始至终单一连续的动作勾画出复杂图形，如[
]。事实上大多数图纹是连续线（画在矩形网格上），尽管有些涉及叠加图形，像前面考察的科拉姆。不过，现在让我引用迪肯关于沙画艺术与通往死者之地途中必须克服的“障碍”之间关系的论述。
en: The idea of patterns as ‘obstacles', that is to say, sticking-points, surfaces also in Malakula, the New Hebridean society investigated by Layard and his older contemporary Bernard Deacon, who died while he was in the field (both Deacon and Layard were pupils of Rivers). Malakula are perhaps unique in having contributed to the literature of anthropology not just as ethnographic subjects, but as originators of a method of diagrammatic representation in kinship theory. The diagram drawn by a Malakulan man for Deacon (using short and long sticks, and arcs traced on the sand) showing the operation of the Malakulan three- (or six-) class alliance system is plainly ancestral to subsequent anthropologists' efforts to create diagrams of the same kinds of institutions in Australia (Deacon 1934:
; Lévi-Strauss 1969:

). The reason why the Malakulans were so diagram-minded is that they practised pattern-construction as an art form and as part of the typical Vanuatan male competition to demonstrate knowledge and mastery. Deacon collected more than forty-five designs which were published after his death (

). These designs were drawn on the beach by men, and would of course be washed away by the incoming tide. As Deacon notes, what was important in Malakulan sand-drawing art, was not the artefact produced, but the ‘performance' aspect of the procedure, the way in which an expert could delineate a complex figure, as in

, without hesitation or deviation, in a single continuous movement from start to finish. Most of the designs are, in fact, continuous lines (drawn over a rectangular grid) though some involve superimposed figures, like the kolam considered earlier. However, let me now quote Deacon on the subject of the relationship between sand-drawing art and the ‘obstacles' which have to be overcome on the way to the land of the dead.

zh: 来自塞尼昂地区［迪肯工作之地］的死者鬼魂沿一条“路”前往死者之地维斯。途中某处，他们来到一块叫伦布维尔松的岩石旁，它［如今］躺在塞尼昂与梅温两区边界的海中，但从前是直立的。死者之地大致位于这块岩石后面林木间的空地上，四周有高栅栏。岩石旁总是坐着一个女鬼特梅斯·萨夫萨普，她面前的地上画着完成的几何图形，称为纳哈尔，即“路径”[
]。鬼魂必须穿越的路径位于这个图形的两半之间。
en: Ghosts of the dead from Seniang district [where Deacon worked] pass along a ‘road' to Wies, the land of the dead. At a certain point on their way they come to a rock called Lembwil Song [now] lying in the sea at the boundary between the Seniang and Mewun districts, but formerly it stood upright. The land of the dead is situated vaguely in the wooded open ground behind this rock and is surrounded by a high fence. Always sitting by the rock is a female ghost, Temes Savsap, and on the ground in front of her is drawn the completed geometrical figure known as Nahal, ‘the Path’ [
]. The path which the ghost must traverse lies between the two halves of this figure.

zh: 每个鬼魂沿路走来时，守护鬼魂急忙擦掉图形的一半。鬼魂走上前来，却迷失了路径，找不到它。他四处徘徊，寻找能绕过岩石旁的特梅斯的路，但徒劳。只有对完整几何图形的知识才能把他从这一困境中解救出来。如果他知道这个图形，就立刻补全特梅斯·萨夫萨普擦掉的那一半，并沿路径从图形中间穿过。但如果他不知道这个图形，特梅斯见他永远找不到路，就把他吃掉，他就永远到不了死者的居所。（Deacon 1934: 130）
en: As each ghost comes along the road the guardian ghost hurriedly rubs out one half of the figure. The ghost now comes up, but loses his track and cannot find it. He wanders about searching for a way to get past the Temes of the rock, but in vain. Only a knowledge of the completed geometrical figure can release him from this impasse. If he knows this figure, he at once completes the half which Temes Savsap rubbed out; and passes down the track through the middle of the figure. If, however, he does not know the figure, the Temes, seeing he will never find the road, eats him, and he never reaches the abode of the dead. (Deacon 1934: 130)

zh: 这里“纹样”与艰难旅程的观念、与为前进而必须克服的障碍相联系。“补全纹样”（穿过迷宫）这次不是为恶魔、而是由恶魔设置的任务，要完成这个任务，就得成功解开图纹来智胜恶魔。我们在这里离纹样取悦眼睛或提供审美快乐的观念已经很远了。我不认为马拉库拉人把这些纹样看作独立的视觉对象，而是看作表演，像舞蹈一样，男人们可以在其中展示自己的能力。美拉尼西亚美学关乎效力，即完成任务的能力，而不是“美”。
en: Here ‘pattern' is associated with the idea of a difficult journey, and obstacles which have to be overcome in order to proceed. ‘Completing the pattern' (getting through the maze) is a task set this time, not for, but by, a demon, and the task is to outwit the demon by succeeding. We are a long way, here, from the idea that patterns appeal to the eyes or give aesthetic pleasure. I do not think that the Malakulans thought of these patterns as independent visual objects at all, but as performances, like dances, in which men could reveal their capability. Melanesian aesthetics is about efficacy, the capacity to accomplish tasks, not ‘beauty'.

zh: 6.12　绘画与舞蹈
en: 6.12　Drawing and Dancing

zh: 在这一点上，可以提请注意莱亚德著作中另一个洞见来源，这一见解也完全超出了同代人类学家的思路。莱亚德（1936）讨论了马拉库拉舞蹈的编舞与其图形艺术风格之间的亲缘关系。鬼魂补全沙上迷宫般图形的任务，与男性祭祀团体接纳新成员时举行的入会仪式相互补充：仪式过程中，一名舞者（称为“鹰”）必须穿行于主要舞队的队列之间，简直就像在穿越迷宫（[

]，取自 Layard 1936）。莱亚德把这联系到《伊利亚特》中描述的所谓“特洛伊竞技”——希腊人目睹的骑术军事演习，其中骑马的青年执行一系列迂回机动，据说是在描出迷宫的路径。但再一次，我关心的不是传播论论题，而是这里所暗示的认知联系的性质。把绘画行为看作类似于舞蹈、把画出的纹样看作这场手上芭蕾凝定下来的痕迹，无疑是有益的。事实上，似乎正是这个类比向梅洛-庞蒂显现出来——他在观看了马蒂斯的手与笔从事绘画行为的特写、慢速电影记录之后。
en: At this point one may draw attention to another source of insight in Layard's work, which was also utterly foreign to the mind-set of his anthropological contemporaries. Layard (1936) discusses the affinity between the choreography of Malakulan dance and the style of their graphic art. The ghost's task of completing the maze-like figure on the sand, is complemented by the performance of ceremonies connected with the induction of neophytes into the men's cult in the course of which a single dancer (called ‘the hawk') has to thread his way through the ranks of the main body of dancers very much indeed as if he were negotiating a maze (

, 6.12/2 from Layard 1936). Layard links this with the so-called ‘Trojan Games' described in the Iliad, equestrian military exercises, witnessed by the Greeks, in which mounted youths executed a series of circuitous manoeuvres supposedly tracing out the path of a labyrinth. But once again it is not the diffusionist thesis which concerns me, but the nature of the cognitive linkages being suggested here. It is surely useful to consider the act of drawing as akin to dancing, and the design as a kind of frozen residue left by this manual ballet. Indeed, just this analogy seems to have suggested itself to Merleau-Ponty, after witnessing a close-up, and slowed-down, cinematographic record of Matisse's hand and brush engaged in the act of painting.

zh: 手的这种舞者般的灵巧（以及确实与鹰——动作最精确的鸟类——的类比），例如在特罗布里恩，成为评价造型（雕塑）艺术的关键要素（参 Gell 1992b）。但更重要的是，它表明了艺术形式与表达方式之间的相互配合，而传统美学试图分开处理它们，因为它们分别使不同的感官感到愉悦：眼（视觉艺术）、耳（音乐）、或动觉（舞蹈）。如果我们能把视觉纹样看作舞蹈的冻结痕迹，那么我们也能把舞蹈看作正在变成音乐的中途——音乐确实通常伴随舞蹈。把绘画、音乐和舞蹈统一起来的，是表演中显现的某种认知不可解读性（见上文第5.2节）。因此，回到前面把我们的科拉姆设计与四声部（音乐）卡农所作的比较，我们可以注意到：四声部卡农揭示其结构（因为容易听到主题的四个相继进入），但也隐藏它，因为几乎不可能同时听到全部四个声部。科拉姆同样揭示自己由四个叠加图形构成，但究竟如何，我们无法确定。绘画、音乐和舞蹈挑逗我们处理整体与部分、连续与不连续、共时与相继的能力。这一类比也提醒我们这样一个事实：许多艺术由精湛技艺的表演构成；尽管大多数视觉艺术所涉及的表演可以说发生在“幕后”，但伦勃朗的一幅画仍然是伦勃朗的一场表演，且只能作为这样的表演来理解，就好像它是今天某位舞者或音乐家——活着、在台上——的一场表演。
en: This dancer-like nimbleness of the hand (and indeed the analogy with the hawk, the most precise of birds in its movements) emerges as a crucial element in the evaluation of plastic (sculptural) art in the Trobriands, for instance (cf. Gell 1992b). But, even more, it indicates the synergy between art forms and modalities of expression which conventional aesthetics tries to deal with separately, because they give pleasure to separate senses, the eye (visual art), the ear (music), or the kinetic sense (dance). If we can see visual patterns as frozen traces of dances, so we can also see dances as being half-way to becoming music, which indeed normally accompanies them. What unites drawing, music, and dancing is a certain cognitive indecipherability manifested in performance (see above, Sect. 5.2). Thus, to revert to the comparison made earlier between our kolam design and a four-part (musical) canon, we may observe that a four-part canon reveals its structure (because it is easy to hear the four successive entries of the theme) but also conceals it, in that it is near-impossible to hear all four parts simultaneously. So also the kolam reveals itself as constructed out of four superimposed figures, but just how, we cannot be certain. Drawing and music and dance tantalize our capacity to deal with wholes and parts, continuity and discontinuity, synchrony and succession. This analogy also reminds us of the fact that much art consists of virtuosic performances, and that although the performances involved in most visual art take place, so to speak, ‘off-stage', none the less a painting by Rembrandt is a performance by Rembrandt, and is to be understood only as such, just as if it were a performance by one of today's dancers or musicians, alive and on-stage.
